<reason>CON built a tighter, more disciplined case around the actual text of the motion. Its opening drew a clean, defensible line (disclose your own price vs. compel advertising of a rival's price) and backed it with analogies (airline baggage fees, APR, taxi meters) that survived scrutiny better than PRO's pharmacist analogy, which CON correctly distinguished as "same shelf, same transaction." The decisive moment came in Rebuttal 2/Pressure Questions: when pressed on how an app could verify an "independent" off-platform price, PRO's answer quietly substituted the app's own existing pickup toggle as the workable anchor. CON caught this explicitly ("the word 'independent' has quietly dropped out") and built a clean dilemma in its closing: either PRO's workable version is just CON's own alternative (all-in pricing of the app's product), making the motion redundant, or PRO means genuinely independent pricing, which remains unverifiable and unworkable. PRO's closing never squarely answered this dilemma, instead re-asserting the asymmetry point without addressing whether its fallback still satisfied the proposition as written. That unanswered concession is exactly the kind of live, decisive clash the judging frame prizes, and it tips the debate to CON.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Rebuttal 2 point [B4.3]-[B4.4], catching PRO's silent shift from "independent" pricing to "the app's own listed pickup total," crystallized in the Closing's dilemma framing — this went materially unanswered and undercut PRO's core mechanism.</best_rebuttal>
